profiles.meeting_scenario: A planning meeting in an ML research lab preparing a 6-week internal benchmark study on how different Design of Experiments (DOE) choices interact with predictive model performance for industrial surrogate modeling. The team wants to turn an existing literature review into a reproducible benchmark that compares 12 DOE strategies, 7 model families, 7 synthetic test functions representing physical processes, and 8 noise settings. The immediate context is that a funding review is coming up, and they need a concrete execution plan for the first benchmark milestone. The agenda is to decide what the 'first pass' benchmark includes, how results will be organized, who handles experiment orchestration versus analysis, and what is expected by the milestone review. The expected outcome is an agreed plan for running the first batch of experiments, preparing an interim results package, and assigning responsibilities without revisiting the already accepted high-level study framing.

members.name: Dr. Elena Rossi
members.expertise: Design of experiments, uncertainty quantification, industrial experimentation
members.background: Elena leads a university-industry collaboration on data-efficient modeling for manufacturing processes and has published extensively on screening designs and response-surface methodology.
members.private_state: She wants a credible interim package for the funding review that looks methodologically complete, while keeping the benchmark manageable enough that the lab can execute it without slipping the review date.
hidden_assumptions: A 'first pass' benchmark still includes the full Cartesian study grid, with lighter reporting depth rather than reduced experimental coverage.
The 'baseline models' are the canonical implementations already used in the lab's prior surrogate-modeling benchmark, with default tuning and one stable software stack.
A 'results table' for the review should contain aggregate rankings and headline summaries, while detailed per-function and per-noise breakdowns can wait for the paper draft.
If they say the package will be 'reproducible,' that means scripts and fixed seeds are sufficient; full containerization and environment capture are publication-stage tasks.

members.name: Kai Verma
members.expertise: ML benchmarking pipelines, experiment automation, reproducibility infrastructure
members.background: Kai maintains the lab's benchmarking framework and has experience translating methodological studies into large automated experiment matrices with tracked environments and standardized outputs.
members.private_state: He wants to avoid another benchmark that becomes impossible to reproduce or rerun, and he prefers narrowing scope early so the pipeline is solid rather than broad but fragile.
hidden_assumptions: A 'first pass' benchmark means a reduced pilot slice of the study grid that validates the pipeline before scaling to all designs, functions, and noise settings.
The 'baseline models' are the current benchmark-framework templates, including the refreshed implementations and preprocessing wrappers introduced this semester.
A 'results table' should include the disaggregated outputs needed to inspect interactions by function class and noise regime, because otherwise the study is not analytically useful.
If the team commits to 'reproducible' experiments, that includes pinned environments, tracked artifacts, and rerunnable configs from the start, not as a later cleanup step.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to do a 'first pass' before the review.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes 'first pass' means running the full 12 x 7 x 7 x 8 benchmark matrix but with minimal interpretation and compact summary tables.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes 'first pass' means running only a pilot subset, such as a few representative designs, a few model families, and selected functions/noise settings to validate the pipeline.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In ML research planning, 'first pass' commonly implies something preliminary, so both hear a familiar phrase and assume the other shares their version of preliminaryness without needing to specify whether scope or analysis depth is what is being reduced.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to start with the 'baseline models' and add the rest later.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is referring to the seven canonical model families as implemented in the lab's older surrogate-study codebase: Gaussian processes, random forests, SVR, MLP, linear models, boosted trees, and k-NN with mostly default settings.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is referring to the benchmark framework's current baseline templates, which map to similar family names but use revised preprocessing, newer library versions, and slightly different default variants.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are experienced enough that 'baseline models' sounds like an established internal object rather than a term requiring unpacking; the family names overlap, so the referential mismatch stays hidden.

misalignment_points.topic: What the interim 'results table' should contain
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that the milestone needs a 'results table' showing which design-model combinations perform best.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 thinks this is satisfied by a concise aggregate ranking across the benchmark, perhaps averaged over functions and noise settings, suitable for slides and review documents.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 thinks this requires stratified outputs showing performance by function type and by homoscedastic versus heteroscedastic settings so that interaction patterns are visible.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both treat 'results table' as a mundane deliverable and assume the obvious standard from their own work context; because both versions would literally be tables of results, neither feels prompted to define the acceptance criteria.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree the benchmark should be 'reproducible from the start.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means fixed random seeds, saved scripts, and a shared experiment folder are enough for the first milestone, with stricter packaging deferred.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the run must already be launched through the tracked pipeline with pinned dependencies, config manifests, and artifact logging so that any result can be rerun exactly.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Reproducibility is a shared value in the lab, so both hear alignment at the principle level; the disagreement is only in the operational threshold, which feels too obvious within each person's professional frame to state explicitly.
